_comment: What `autovec` means in this project, as data.
`autovec` is not a code tier: the scalar bodies are the implementation and the only thing
that can be true or false is whether the shipped flags vectorise them. `isa_gate.py`
recompiles each file below with `flags` and counts packed SSE2 instructions in the
disassembly, so the claim is re-measured on every run instead of being remembered.
Measured 2026-11-26 on gcc 13 (x86-64), packed instruction counts with -O2 vs -O3:
add.c   0 -> 5    relu.c  0 -> 5    scale.c 0 -> 8    fc.c 0 -> 7    quant.c 1 -> 30
reduce.c 1 -> 1 (unchanged)
This falsifies the earlier note that the kernel ABI blocks vectorisation: -O2 does, -O3
does not, and `restrict`/`ivdep` make no difference at -O3. CMake's Release flags are
-O3 -DNDEBUG, which is why the shipped release build already gets these.
`degraded` is not a to-do list: it records where the tier is honestly *absent* and why.
It exists so that a missing vectorisation cannot be silently dropped from this file --
an entry without a reason is red.
Second claim (2026-11-26): the hand-written tiers are measured too, but at -O0.
-O0 turns the auto-vectoriser off, so a packed instruction there can only come from an
explicit intrinsic: that is what separates "this body uses the ISA" from "this body happens
to be vectorisable". Parity tests cannot see the difference -- a scalar loop returns the same
values -- which is why this had to be a disassembly rule rather than a test.
Measured 2026-11-26 at -O0 (ISA-specific mnemonics, see the gate for the patterns):
x86      add 10  fc 20  fc_i8 84  fc_i16 133  reduce 30  relu 19  relu_i8 20  scale 11  sum 14
arm_neon add 3   fc 7   reduce 7  relu 8      scale 4    sum 9   relu_i8 4
rvv      add 9   fc 14  reduce 12 relu 7      relu_i8 7  scale 7 sum 12
arm_m    fc 2 (SMLAD/SMLALD)         every register.c: 0 (it is a table, not a body)
min_packed is 1 for every body on purpose: the claim is boolean ("this body uses its ISA"),
and a floor above it would make ordinary edits red without adding information. `measured`
records what the number was, so drift shows up in the gate output instead of being forgotten.
The cross tiers SKIP with a reason when their compiler is absent (the CI job has no Conan
cache); a SKIP is printed, never absorbed into the OK line.

src/kernel/scalar/add.c.what: fp32 elementwise add; measured 5 packed instructions

src/kernel/scalar/fc.c.what: fp32 and int8/int16 dot products; measured 7

degraded.src/kernel/scalar/reduce.c: sum would need reassociation (-ffast-math) to become a packed reduction, and that changes the answer the parity window is defined against; max folds with a NaN-sensitive `>` and stays scalar. Measured 1 packed instruction before and after -O3, i.e. neither kernel becomes a packed reduction.

src/kernel/arm_neon/fc_i16.c.what: int16 dot: widening multiply then int64 accumulate

src/kernel/arm_neon/fc_i8.c.what: int8 dot: vmull_s8 + vpadalq_s16, int32 accumulate

src/kernel/arm_neon/quant.c.what: int8 to fp32 dequantize (integer subtract + one IEEE multiply)

src/kernel/rvv/fc.c.what: fp32 dot with a vector accumulator

src/kernel/rvv/fc_i16.c.what: int16 dot: e16m1 -> e32m2 -> e64m4, exact int64 lanes

src/kernel/rvv/fc_i8.c.what: int8 dot: e8m1 -> e16m2 then vwmacc into int32

src/kernel/rvv/quant.c.what: quantize (IEEE divide, round, clamp) and dequantize

src/kernel/x86/fc_i16.c.what: int16 dot: zero-interleaved maddwd, int64 accumulate

src/kernel/x86/fc_i8.c.what: int8 dot: sign mask, unpack to int16, maddwd

src/kernel/x86/reduce.c.what: max and sum, compare+select so NaN/order match

src/kernel/x86/relu.c.what: fp32 relu via cmpgt+and, not maxps

excluded.src/kernel/x86/register.c: registry table only (a list of descriptors), no kernel body
excluded.src/kernel/arm_neon/register.c: registry table only, no kernel body
excluded.src/kernel/rvv/register.c: registry table only, no kernel body
excluded.src/kernel/arm_m/register.c: registry table only, no kernel body
